summary: First checkpoint of the blueprint for Euler systems and the unconditional cyclotomic main conjecture. It decomposes layer L0 from Rubin's Euler systems (Chapter III §2.1–2.4 with the Chapter I–II definitions it uses) and RJW §10.2 and §10.5. The layer contains: the distribution relation for 1 − ζ over any cyclotomic step, with the sign dictionary to Rubin's ζ − 1 form (whose ℓ = 2 case is wrong as printed); the p-extended cyclotomic numbers c̃_m and their real norms, with the tower and auxiliary-prime relations and non-torsion; the comparison with the smoothed units c(a) and the smoothing divisor θ_a; the Kummer classes and the theorem that they form an Euler system for (ℤ_p(1), ℚ^ab, p); χ-components and twisted sums; the χ-cyclotomic generators and units; and Rubin's c_ℚ = ξ_{L,χ}^{1 − χ^{−1}(p)}. The carrier, the tower and the cohomology are imported by six requests. Layers L1–L4 are not yet read.

nodes.title: Minimal polynomial of a cyclotomic step when ℓ divides m
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be prime with ℓ ∣ m, K = ℚ(μ_m) ⊆ L = ℚ(μ_{mℓ}), ζ ∈ L a primitive mℓ-th root of unity and η = ζ^ℓ ∈ K. Then the minimal polynomial of ζ over K is X^ℓ − η.
hypotheses: ℓ is prime and m ≥ 1; K and L are cyclotomic over ℚ of conductors m and mℓ (Mathlib's IsCyclotomicExtension {m} ℚ K and {mℓ} ℚ L), with L a K-algebra.
ζ ∈ L is a primitive mℓ-th root of unity and η ∈ K satisfies η = ζ^ℓ in L, so η is a primitive m-th root; this is the compatibility ζ_{mℓ}^ℓ = ζ_m that Rubin fixes before (2).
ℓ ∣ m.
proofSteps: [L : ℚ] = φ(mℓ) = ℓ·φ(m) because ℓ ∣ m (Nat.totient_mul_of_prime_of_dvd), and [K : ℚ] = φ(m); both from IsCyclotomicExtension.finrank with the irreducibility of the rational cyclotomic polynomials.
By the tower law (Module.finrank_mul_finrank), [L : K] = ℓ. L is generated over ℚ, hence over K, by ζ, so deg minpoly_K(ζ) = ℓ (IntermediateField.adjoin.finrank).
ζ is a root of the monic degree-ℓ polynomial X^ℓ − η ∈ K[X], so minpoly_K(ζ) divides it (minpoly.dvd); both are monic of degree ℓ, so they are equal.
acceptance: m = 2, ℓ = 2: the minimal polynomial of i over ℚ is X² + 1 = X² − ζ₂.
m = p^{n−1}, ℓ = p: this is RJW's X^p − ξ_{p^{n−1}} in the proof of Lemma 10.3.

nodes.title: Minimal polynomial of a cyclotomic step when ℓ does not divide m
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be prime with ℓ ∤ m, and let ℓ' satisfy ℓℓ' ≡ 1 (mod m). With K, L, ζ, η as before, η^{ℓ'} ∈ K is a root of X^ℓ − η, and minpoly_K(ζ)·(X − η^{ℓ'}) = X^ℓ − η. So the conjugates of ζ over K are the ℓ-th roots of η other than η^{ℓ'}, the unique one of order dividing m.
hypotheses: ℓ is prime and m ≥ 1; K and L are cyclotomic over ℚ of conductors m and mℓ (Mathlib's IsCyclotomicExtension {m} ℚ K and {mℓ} ℚ L), with L a K-algebra.
ζ ∈ L is a primitive mℓ-th root of unity and η ∈ K satisfies η = ζ^ℓ in L, so η is a primitive m-th root; this is the compatibility ζ_{mℓ}^ℓ = ζ_m that Rubin fixes before (2).
ℓ ∤ m and ℓℓ' ≡ 1 (mod m); for m = 1 every ℓ' works and η = 1.
proofSteps: [L : ℚ] = φ(m)(ℓ − 1) (Nat.totient_mul for coprime m, ℓ, and φ(ℓ) = ℓ − 1), so [L : K] = ℓ − 1 by the tower law.
(η^{ℓ'})^ℓ = η^{ℓℓ'} = η because η^m = 1, so X − η^{ℓ'} divides X^ℓ − η in K[X]; the quotient g is monic of degree ℓ − 1.
ζ ≠ η^{ℓ'} since ζ has order mℓ and η^{ℓ'} has order dividing m, so g(ζ) = 0; hence minpoly_K(ζ) divides g, and equality follows from the degrees.
acceptance: m = 3, ℓ = 2: L = ℚ(μ_6) = K, and minpoly is X − ζ_6 with ζ_6 = −ζ_3² (the other root of X² − ζ_3 is ζ_3², the one of order 3).

nodes.title: Distribution relation, ℓ dividing m
nodes.statement: With K = ℚ(μ_m) ⊆ L = ℚ(μ_{mℓ}), ζ = ζ_{mℓ}, η = ζ^ℓ = ζ_m and ℓ ∣ m: N_{L/K}(1 − ζ) = 1 − η.
hypotheses: ℓ is prime and m ≥ 1; K and L are cyclotomic over ℚ of conductors m and mℓ (Mathlib's IsCyclotomicExtension {m} ℚ K and {mℓ} ℚ L), with L a K-algebra.
ζ ∈ L is a primitive mℓ-th root of unity and η ∈ K satisfies η = ζ^ℓ in L, so η is a primitive m-th root; this is the compatibility ζ_{mℓ}^ℓ = ζ_m that Rubin fixes before (2).
ℓ ∣ m.
The 1 − ζ convention; Rubin's ζ − 1 form differs by (−1)^ℓ (distribution-relation-rubin-convention).
proofSteps: L/K is Galois (cyclotomic), so N_{L/K}(1 − ζ) = ∏_{σ ∈ Gal(L/K)} (1 − σζ) (Algebra.norm_eq_prod_automorphisms).
The σζ are the roots of minpoly_K(ζ) = X^ℓ − η, each once, so the product is the value of X^ℓ − η at X = 1, namely 1 − η.

nodes.title: Distribution relation, ℓ not dividing m
nodes.statement: With K = ℚ(μ_m) ⊆ L = ℚ(μ_{mℓ}), ζ = ζ_{mℓ}, η = ζ_m, ℓ ∤ m and ℓℓ' ≡ 1 (mod m): N_{L/K}(1 − ζ)·(1 − η^{ℓ'}) = 1 − η. For m > 1 both factors are nonzero, so N_{L/K}(1 − ζ_{mℓ}) = (1 − ζ_m)^{1 − Fr_ℓ^{−1}}, Fr_ℓ^{−1} acting by ζ_m ↦ ζ_m^{ℓ'}.
hypotheses: ℓ is prime and m ≥ 1; K and L are cyclotomic over ℚ of conductors m and mℓ (Mathlib's IsCyclotomicExtension {m} ℚ K and {mℓ} ℚ L), with L a K-algebra.
ζ ∈ L is a primitive mℓ-th root of unity and η ∈ K satisfies η = ζ^ℓ in L, so η is a primitive m-th root; this is the compatibility ζ_{mℓ}^ℓ = ζ_m that Rubin fixes before (2).
ℓ ∤ m and ℓℓ' ≡ 1 (mod m).
For m = 1 the identity reads 0 = 0; the conductor-one value is distribution-relation-conductor-one.
proofSteps: N_{L/K}(1 − ζ) = ∏_σ (1 − σζ) (Algebra.norm_eq_prod_automorphisms), and the σζ are the roots of minpoly_K(ζ).
Evaluate minpoly_K(ζ)·(X − η^{ℓ'}) = X^ℓ − η (minpoly-step-of-not-dvd) at X = 1.
acceptance: The relation holds for every prime ℓ, including ℓ = 2, with no sign; the ζ − 1 form of Rubin's (2) fails at ℓ = 2 (sourceIssues E1).

nodes.title: Distribution relation with the arithmetic Frobenius
nodes.statement: Let σ ∈ Gal(ℚ(μ_m)/ℚ) be the inverse of the arithmetic Frobenius Fr_ℓ (ζ_m ↦ ζ_m^ℓ), that is the image of ℓ^{−1} ∈ (ℤ/m)^× under Mathlib's autEquivPow. For ℓ ∤ m, N_{ℚ(μ_{mℓ})/ℚ(μ_m)}(1 − ζ_{mℓ})·σ(1 − ζ_m) = 1 − ζ_m.
hypotheses: ℓ is prime and m ≥ 1; K and L are cyclotomic over ℚ of conductors m and mℓ (Mathlib's IsCyclotomicExtension {m} ℚ K and {mℓ} ℚ L), with L a K-algebra.
ζ ∈ L is a primitive mℓ-th root of unity and η ∈ K satisfies η = ζ^ℓ in L, so η is a primitive m-th root; this is the compatibility ζ_{mℓ}^ℓ = ζ_m that Rubin fixes before (2).
ℓ is coprime to m.
proofSteps: σ(ζ_m) = ζ_m^{ℓ'} for any ℓ' ≡ ℓ^{−1} (mod m), by the defining property of autEquivPow.
Substitute into distribution-relation-of-not-dvd.
acceptance: Fr_ℓ is the arithmetic Frobenius, as in Rubin and in RJW Definition 10.16 (σ_ℓ the image of Frob_ℓ); the Euler factor involves Fr_ℓ^{−1}.

nodes.title: The ζ − 1 convention and its sign
nodes.statement: For any finite field extension L/K and ζ ∈ L, N_{L/K}(ζ − 1) = (−1)^{[L:K]} N_{L/K}(1 − ζ). Hence, for the cyclotomic step, N(ζ_{mℓ} − 1) = (−1)^{ℓ+1}(ζ_m − 1) if ℓ ∣ m and N(ζ_{mℓ} − 1) = (−1)^{ℓ−1}(ζ_m − 1)^{1 − Fr_ℓ^{−1}} if ℓ ∤ m, m > 1. For odd ℓ these are Rubin's formulas (2); for ℓ = 2 his first two cases need the sign −1.
hypotheses: [L : K] = ℓ when ℓ ∣ m and ℓ − 1 when ℓ ∤ m (the two minimal-polynomial nodes).
proofSteps: N is multiplicative and N_{L/K}(−1) = (−1)^{[L:K]} (the norm of an element of K is its [L:K]-th power, Algebra.norm_algebraMap).
Combine with distribution-relation-of-dvd and distribution-relation-of-not-dvd.
acceptance: Counterexample to the printed (2) at ℓ = 2: N_{ℚ(i)/ℚ}(i − 1) = 2 while ζ_2 − 1 = −2.
Second counterexample: ℓ = 2, m = 3 gives ζ_6 − 1 = ζ_3 while (ζ_3 − 1)^{1 − Fr_2^{−1}} = −ζ_3.

nodes.title: Distribution relation at conductor one
nodes.statement: For every prime ℓ and primitive ℓ-th root ζ_ℓ, N_{ℚ(μ_ℓ)/ℚ}(1 − ζ_ℓ) = ℓ; equivalently N(ζ_ℓ − 1) = (−1)^{ℓ−1}ℓ, Rubin's third case.
hypotheses: ℓ prime, including ℓ = 2 where ℚ(μ_2) = ℚ and ζ_2 = −1.
proofSteps: For ℓ odd, N(ζ − 1) = Φ_ℓ(1) = ℓ (IsPrimitiveRoot.sub_one_norm_eq_eval_cyclotomic with 2 < ℓ, and Polynomial.eval_one_cyclotomic_prime), and N(1 − ζ) = (−1)^{ℓ−1}N(ζ − 1) = ℓ (distribution-relation-rubin-convention).

nodes.title: The p-extended cyclotomic numbers c̃_m
nodes.statement: Fix a prime p and the compatible roots ζ_m with the tower ℚ(μ_m) (requested from IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0). For m ≥ 1 put c̃_m = N_{ℚ(μ_{mp})/ℚ(μ_m)}(1 − ζ_{mp}) ∈ ℚ(μ_m)^×. This is Rubin's c̃_{m∞} in the 1 − ζ convention: Rubin's element N(ζ_{mp} − 1) equals (−1)^{[ℚ(μ_{mp}):ℚ(μ_m)]}c̃_m.
hypotheses: p prime; m ≥ 1. No coprimality between m and p is assumed.
The extra norm from level mp is what makes the family norm-compatible in the p-direction (Rubin, Remark 2.1); it loses information when p ∤ m.
proofSteps: Definition as a relative norm.

API: c̃_m = 1 − ζ_m if p ∣ m (distribution-relation-of-dvd with ℓ = p); c̃_1 = p (distribution-relation-conductor-one); c̃_m ≠ 0 (1 − ζ_{mp} ≠ 0 as mp > 1); the Rubin sign (distribution-relation-rubin-convention).
acceptance: The family is not torsion (p-extended-nontorsion), unlike RJW's (ξ^{−1} − 1)/(ξ − 1) = −ξ^{−1}.
Individual c̃_m can be torsion: for p = 5, c̃_3 = −ζ_3.

nodes.title: Tower relation for c̃
nodes.statement: For every m ≥ 1, N_{ℚ(μ_{mp})/ℚ(μ_m)}(c̃_{mp}) = c̃_m.
hypotheses: m ≥ 1, p prime.
proofSteps: c̃_{mp} = 1 − ζ_{mp} since p ∣ mp (pCycNumber_of_dvd, from distribution-relation-of-dvd).
The left side is then N(1 − ζ_{mp}) = c̃_m by definition.
acceptance: This is the Euler-system relation at ℓ = p, where no Euler factor enters (N is divisible by p).

nodes.title: Auxiliary-prime relation for c̃
nodes.statement: For a prime ℓ ≠ p and m ≥ 1: N_{ℚ(μ_{mℓ})/ℚ(μ_m)}(c̃_{mℓ}) = c̃_m^{1 − Fr_ℓ^{−1}} if ℓ ∤ m, and = c̃_m if ℓ ∣ m. Here Fr_ℓ ∈ Gal(ℚ(μ_m)/ℚ). The case m = 1 is included (then Fr_ℓ = 1 and the norm is 1).
hypotheses: ℓ prime, ℓ ≠ p; m ≥ 1.
The conductor-one exception of (2) never occurs, because c̃ is a norm from level mp > 1.
proofSteps: Norms are transitive in the square ℚ(μ_m) ⊆ ℚ(μ_{mp}), ℚ(μ_{mℓ}) ⊆ ℚ(μ_{mℓp}) (Algebra.norm_norm), so the left side is N_{ℚ(μ_{mp})/ℚ(μ_m)}(N_{ℚ(μ_{mℓp})/ℚ(μ_{mp})}(1 − ζ_{mℓp})).
Apply distribution-relation-of-dvd (ℓ ∣ mp) or distribution-relation-frobenius (ℓ ∤ mp) at level mp.
The norm N_{ℚ(μ_{mp})/ℚ(μ_m)} commutes with the Galois action (the extensions are abelian), and Fr_ℓ on ℚ(μ_{mp}) restricts to Fr_ℓ on ℚ(μ_m) (IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0).
acceptance: Checked numerically for p ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7}, m < 30 and ℓ ≤ 13: 812 cases, no failure, including p = 2 and ℓ = 2.

nodes.title: The cyclotomic family is not torsion
nodes.statement: c̃_1 = p, and for k ≥ 1, c̃_{p^k} = 1 − ζ_{p^k} with N_{ℚ(μ_{p^k})/ℚ}(1 − ζ_{p^k}) = p. Neither is of finite order, since roots of unity have norm ±1.
hypotheses: p prime, k ≥ 1.
proofSteps: c̃_{p^k} = 1 − ζ_{p^k} (pCycNumber_of_dvd).
Iterating distribution-relation-of-dvd down the tower and using Algebra.norm_norm, N_{ℚ(μ_{p^k})/ℚ(μ_p)}(1 − ζ_{p^k}) = 1 − ζ_p; then distribution-relation-conductor-one gives p.
A root of unity has norm a root of unity in ℚ, that is ±1 ≠ p.
acceptance: Contrast: RJW's c_m = −ξ_m^{−1} is a root of unity (sourceIssues E2).

nodes.title: Relations for the real cyclotomic numbers
nodes.statement: The family c̃^+ satisfies the relations of c̃: N_{ℚ(μ_{mp})^+/ℚ(μ_m)^+}(c̃_{mp}^+) = c̃_m^+, and for a prime ℓ ≠ p, N_{ℚ(μ_{mℓ})^+/ℚ(μ_m)^+}(c̃_{mℓ}^+) = (c̃_m^+)^{1 − Fr_ℓ^{−1}} if ℓ ∤ m and = c̃_m^+ if ℓ ∣ m. Moreover N_{ℚ(μ_m)/ℚ(μ_m)^+}(c̃_m) = c̃_m^+ by definition, the relation between conductors m∞ and m.
hypotheses: m ≥ 1; ℓ ≠ p prime.
proofSteps: N_{ℚ(μ_m)/ℚ(μ_m)^+} commutes with the norms between levels, by transitivity in the square of real and full cyclotomic fields (Algebra.norm_norm), and with the Galois action.
Apply p-extended-tower-relation and p-extended-auxiliary-relation.
acceptance: Both relations are proved simultaneously by the same commutation.

nodes.title: Smoothed cyclotomic units and the smoothing divisor
nodes.statement: Let m ≥ 2 and a ∈ ℕ coprime to m. Then c_m(a) = (1 − ζ_m^a)/(1 − ζ_m) = ∑_{i<a} ζ_m^i is a unit of ℤ[ζ_m] and equals σ_a(1 − ζ_m)/(1 − ζ_m). If p ∣ m it equals σ_a(c̃_m)/c̃_m = c̃_m^{σ_a − 1}; for m = p^n it is RJW's c_n(a) = (ξ^a − 1)/(ξ − 1). The operator σ_a − 1 is the image of the smoothing divisor θ_a = δ_a − δ_1 (the denominator of DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-pseudomeasure) under the finite projection Λ(ℤ_p^×) → ℤ_p[(ℤ/p^n)^×] ≅ ℤ_p[Gal(ℚ(μ_{p^n})/ℚ)], δ_u ↦ σ_{u mod p^n}. The smoothed family {c̃_m^{σ_a − 1} : (m, a) = 1} satisfies the relations of p-extended-tower-relation and p-extended-auxiliary-relation for the primes ℓ ∤ a.
hypotheses: m ≥ 2 and gcd(a, m) = 1; a need not be prime to p for the unit statement, but the family indexed by all m requires the primes dividing a to be excluded, since σ_a is defined only on ℚ(μ_m) with (a, m) = 1.
a = ±1 gives the torsion elements 1 and −ζ_m^{−1}; the nondegenerate smoothing uses a ∉ {0, ±1}.
proofSteps: The quotient is the geometric sum, a unit by IsPrimitiveRoot.geom_sum_isUnit.
σ_a(1 − ζ_m) = 1 − ζ_m^a by definition of σ_a (IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0); for p ∣ m use pCycNumber_of_dvd.

Under the finite projection (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/finite-projection-algebra-map) with the Dirac homomorphism (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/dirac-hom) and unit reduction (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/unit-reduction), δ_a − δ_1 maps to [a mod p^n] − [1], which acts as σ_a − 1.
σ_a commutes with the relative norms, so the relations transfer.
acceptance: The signs of the ζ − 1 and 1 − ζ conventions cancel in the quotient.

nodes.title: ℚ^ab and N = p satisfy the Euler-system hypotheses
nodes.statement: The pair (𝒦, N) = (ℚ^ab, p) satisfies Rubin's Definition II.1.1: (i) 𝒦 contains ℚ(q) for every prime q ≠ p; (ii) 𝒦 contains the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension ℚ_∞, in which no finite prime splits completely. In the conductor-indexed presentation of Remark II.1.3, the fields are 𝒦 ∩ ℚ[m∞] = ℚ(μ_m) and 𝒦 ∩ ℚ[m] = ℚ(μ_m)^+.
hypotheses: p prime (Rubin's §2.1 takes any p; the applications take p > 2).
proofSteps: (i) ℚ(q) lies in the ray class field modulo q, which is ℚ(μ_q)^+ ⊆ ℚ^ab (class field theory over ℚ).

(ii) ℚ_∞ ⊆ ℚ(μ_{p^∞}) ⊆ ℚ^ab with Gal(ℚ_∞/ℚ) ≅ ℤ_p; p is totally ramified, and for q ≠ p the Frobenius of q has image q in ℤ_p^×, which is not a root of unity, so its image in ℤ_p has infinite order and the decomposition group is infinite (Rubin, Remark II.1.2).
The ray class fields of ℚ modulo m∞ and m are ℚ(μ_m) and ℚ(μ_m)^+.
acceptance: Every hypothesis of Definition II.1.1 is checked for this 𝒦 and N, not assumed.

nodes.title: Kummer classes of the cyclotomic numbers
nodes.statement: For N ≥ 0 and m ≥ 1, κ_N(c̃_m) ∈ H¹(G_{ℚ(μ_m)}, μ_{p^N}) is the Tau Ceti Kummer class of c̃_m (TauCeti.kummerMap, n = p^N invertible in characteristic 0), and likewise κ_N(c̃_m^+) over ℚ(μ_m)^+. The classes are compatible in N, and define κ(c̃_m) ∈ H¹(ℚ(μ_m), ℤ_p(1)) = lim_N H¹(ℚ(μ_m), μ_{p^N}) = (ℚ(μ_m)^×)^, Rubin's (1).
hypotheses: p prime; p^N is invertible in every number field.
The inverse limit and the identification with the p-adic completion are requested from SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0.
proofSteps: Apply TauCeti.kummerMap to c̃_m and c̃_m^+.
Compatibility in N: the p-th power map μ_{p^{N+1}} → μ_{p^N} commutes with the Kummer maps (connecting maps of compatible Kummer sequences; SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0).

For every m and prime q ≠ p, Cor κ(c̃_{mq}) = P(Fr_q^{−1} | ℤ_p(1)^*; Fr_q^{−1}) κ(c̃_m) = (1 − Fr_q^{−1})κ(c̃_m) if q ∤ m and = κ(c̃_m) if q ∣ m; Cor κ(c̃_{mp}) = κ(c̃_m); the same holds for c̃^+; and Cor_{ℚ(μ_m)/ℚ(μ_m)^+} κ(c̃_m) = κ(c̃_m^+). hypotheses: p prime, 𝒦 = ℚ^ab, N = p.
ℤ_p(1)^* = Hom(ℤ_p(1), ℤ_p(1)) = ℤ_p with trivial action, so P(Fr_q^{−1}|T^*; x) = 1 − x.

Kummer classes turn norms into corestrictions (cyclotomic-kummer-classes).

nodes.title: χ-components
nodes.statement: Let O be a commutative ring, Δ a finite group, M an O[Δ]-module and χ : Δ → O^× a character. The χ-component is M^χ = {x ∈ M : δx = χ(δ)x for all δ ∈ Δ}, an O-submodule. For a ℤ[Δ]-module B, Rubin's B^χ is (B̂ ⊗_{ℤ_p} O)^χ, with B̂ the p-adic completion (B ⊗ ℤ_p for B finitely generated). Equivalently B^χ ≅ (B̂ ⊗ O_{χ^{−1}})^Δ after fixing a generator of O_{χ^{−1}}.
hypotheses: For exactness and the decomposition B̂ ⊗ O = ⊕_χ B^χ, |Δ| must be invertible in O (Rubin: [L : K] prime to p) and O must contain the values of all characters.
When p divides |Δ| the character functors are those of layer L4 (Greither); this node is the prime-to-p case.
proofSteps: Definition as an eigen-submodule; closure under 0, + and O-scalars uses only that O is commutative.
The twist description is Mathlib's invariants (Representation.invariants) of ρ ⊗ χ^{−1}.
Exactness and the decomposition use the idempotents |Δ|^{−1}∑ χ(δ)^{−1}δ (chi-sum), as for Representation.averageMap.
acceptance: The trivial character gives the invariants.

nodes.title: The χ-cyclotomic generators ξ_{n,χ}
nodes.statement: Let χ be an even nontrivial character of G_ℚ of finite order prime to p, with conductor f, fixed field L and Δ = Gal(L/ℚ); let ℚ_n ⊆ ℚ(μ_{p^{n+1}}) be the layers of ℚ_∞ and L_n = Lℚ_n, so Gal(L_n/ℚ_n) = Δ. Put u_0 = N_{ℚ(μ_f)/L}(1 − ζ_f) and, for n > 0, u_n = N_{ℚ(μ_{fp^{n+1}})/L_n}(1 − ζ_{fp^{n+1}}). Then ξ_{n,χ} = chiSum_χ(1 ⊗ u_n) ∈ (O ⊗ L_n^×)^χ. It equals Rubin's ∏_{δ∈Gal(ℚ(μ_f)/ℚ)} (ζ_f^δ − 1)^{χ^{−1}(δ)} (n = 0), respectively the product over Gal(ℚ_n(μ_{fp^{n+1}})/ℚ_n) (n > 0).
hypotheses: χ even, nontrivial, of order prime to p (Rubin §III.2.2); χ is viewed as a Dirichlet character modulo f with χ(q) = 0 for q ∣ f.
The sign convention is immaterial: ∑ χ^{−1}(δ) = 0 over each group, since χ is nontrivial on it, so (−1) contributes (−1)^0.
proofSteps: Rewrite Rubin's product over Gal(ℚ(μ_f)/ℚ) by grouping δ by its restriction to L: χ^{−1}(δ) depends only on δ|_L, and the inner product is the norm to L. This keeps ξ in L_n^× ⊗ O without a descent step (p may divide [ℚ(μ_f) : L]).
chiSum lands in the χ-component (chiSum_mem).
acceptance: For χ the quadratic character of conductor 5 and p = 3: L = ℚ(√5), u_0 = (1 − ζ_5)(1 − ζ_5^{−1}) = (5 − √5)/2 and ξ_{L,χ} = u_0/σ(u_0) = (3 − √5)/2 = ε^{−2}, with ε = (1 + √5)/2.

nodes.title: The twisted class c_ℚ
nodes.statement: Let c = c̃^{χ^{−1}} be the twist by χ^{−1} of the Euler system of cyclotomic units (ES.2, Rubin Proposition II.4.2), an Euler system for (T^*, ℚ^ab, pf) with T = O_χ, T^* = ℤ_p(1) ⊗ χ^{−1}. Under the restriction–Kummer isomorphism H¹(ℚ, T^*) ≅ (L^×)^χ ⊆ L^× ⊗̂ O (Rubin (3)), c_ℚ corresponds to chiSum_χ(1 ⊗ N_{ℚ(μ_{fp})/L}(1 − ζ_{fp})) = ∏_{δ∈Gal(ℚ(μ_{fp})/ℚ)} (1 − ζ_{fp}^δ)^{χ^{−1}(δ)}.
hypotheses: χ even, nontrivial, of order prime to p, conductor f; [L : ℚ] prime to p.
proofSteps: ES.2's twisting lemma (Rubin Lemma II.4.3) with F = ℚ and L' = ℚ(μ_f)^+, which has the same conductor as L because χ is even, gives ∏_{δ∈Gal(ℚ(μ_f)^+/ℚ)} (δc̃_f^+)^{χ^{−1}(δ)}.
c̃_f^+ = N_{ℚ(μ_f)/ℚ(μ_f)^+}N_{ℚ(μ_{fp})/ℚ(μ_f)}(1 − ζ_{fp}), so the product is the one over Gal(ℚ(μ_{fp})/ℚ); the sign convention is immaterial for χ ≠ 1.
acceptance: For p ∣ f the norm N_{ℚ(μ_{fp})/ℚ(μ_f)}(1 − ζ_{fp}) is 1 − ζ_f.

nodes.title: c_ℚ = ξ_{L,χ}^{1 − χ^{−1}(p)}
nodes.statement: With χ as above and χ(p) = 0 when p ∣ f: c_ℚ = ξ_{L,χ}^{1 − χ^{−1}(p)} in (L^×)^χ, that is chiSum_χ(1 ⊗ N_{ℚ(μ_{fp})/L}(1 − ζ_{fp})) = (1 − χ^{−1}(p))·ξ_{L,χ}.
hypotheses: χ even, nontrivial, of order prime to p, conductor f.
proofSteps: By twisted-class-formula, c_ℚ is chiSum_χ(1 ⊗ u') with u' = N_{ℚ(μ_f)/L}(N_{ℚ(μ_{fp})/ℚ(μ_f)}(1 − ζ_{fp})).

If p ∤ f, the inner norm is (1 − ζ_f)^{1 − Fr_p^{−1}} (distribution-relation-frobenius), so u' = u_0 − Fr_p^{−1}u_0 additively; chi-sum-frobenius with φ = Fr_p|_L gives (1 − χ(Fr_p)^{−1})ξ_{L,χ} = (1 − χ^{−1}(p))ξ_{L,χ}.
If p ∣ f, the inner norm is 1 − ζ_f (distribution-relation-of-dvd), so c_ℚ = ξ_{L,χ} = ξ_{L,χ}^{1 − 0}.
acceptance: For χ(p) = 1 the class c_ℚ is trivial: this is the source of Rubin's hypothesis χ(p) ≠ 1 (Remark III.2.1).

nodes.statement: If χ(p) ≠ 1, then 1 − χ^{−1}(p) ∈ O^× and c_ℚ generates C_{L,χ} = O·ξ_{L,χ}.
hypotheses: χ of order prime to p, χ(p) ≠ 1 (including χ(p) = 0 when p ∣ f).
proofSteps: χ^{−1}(p) is 0 or a root of unity ω ≠ 1 of order dividing ord χ, prime to p; then one-sub-root-of-unity-unit makes 1 − ω a unit.
c_ℚ = (1 − χ^{−1}(p))ξ_{L,χ} (twisted-class-eq-xi-power) and C_{L,χ} = O·ξ_{L,χ} (chi-cyclotomic-units).
acceptance: For χ(p) = 1 the conclusion fails: c_ℚ = 0.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter III, §2.1, display (2), printed p. 34 (PDF p. 44); also Remark 2.1 for p = 2
sourceIssues.printed: The source gives, for each m ≥ 1 and each prime ℓ, N_{Q(µmℓ)/Q(µm)}(ζmℓ − 1) = (ζm − 1) if ℓ | m; (ζm − 1)^{1−Fr_ℓ^{−1}} if ℓ ∤ m and m > 1; (−1)^{ℓ−1}ℓ if m = 1. Here Frℓ denotes the Frobenius attached to ℓ in Gal(Q(µm)/Q).
sourceIssues.correction: N(ζ_{mℓ} − 1) = (−1)^{ℓ+1}(ζ_m − 1) if ℓ ∣ m and (−1)^{ℓ−1}(ζ_m − 1)^{1 − Fr_ℓ^{−1}} if ℓ ∤ m, m > 1. Equivalently, in the 1 − ζ convention: N(1 − ζ_{mℓ}) = 1 − ζ_m, (1 − ζ_m)^{1 − Fr_ℓ^{−1}}, and ℓ for m = 1, with no sign. The printed formula holds for odd ℓ.
sourceIssues.reason: N(ζ − 1) = (−1)^d N(1 − ζ) with d = [ℚ(μ_{mℓ}) : ℚ(μ_m)] = ℓ or ℓ − 1, and the 1 − ζ form has no sign. For ℓ = m = 2: N_{ℚ(i)/ℚ}(i − 1) = (i − 1)(−i − 1) = 2, while ζ_2 − 1 = −2. For ℓ = 2, m = 3: ℚ(μ_6) = ℚ(μ_3) and ζ_6 − 1 = ζ_3, while (ζ_3 − 1)^{1 − Fr_2^{−1}} = −ζ_3. A numerical check over m < 40 and ℓ ≤ 13 finds failures exactly at ℓ = 2. Remark 2.1's 'c̃_{m∞} = ζ_m − 1 for p ∣ m' inherits the sign at p = 2. The Euler-system conclusions are unaffected: for odd p, −1 is a p^N-th power, so the sign vanishes in H¹(F, ℤ_p(1)), and ℓ = 2 occurs only as an auxiliary prime.

sourceIssues.printed: With m = Dp^n, n ≥ 1, the source sets c_m := (ξ_m^{−1} − 1)/(ξ_m − 1) ∈ O^×_{Q(µm)}, extending the units c_n(−1) of Example 10.2 for D = 1. It claims N_{Q(µmℓ)/Q(µm)}(c_{mℓ}) = c_m if ℓ | m, (1 − ℓ^{−1})c_m if ℓ ∤ m.
sourceIssues.correction: Use c_m(a) = (ξ_m^a − 1)/(ξ_m − 1) for a fixed integer a ∉ {0, ±1}, over the m prime to a (the primes dividing a join Σ), or Rubin's unsmoothed N_{ℚ(μ_{mp})/ℚ(μ_m)}(1 − ξ_{mp}). For ℓ ∤ m (and ℓ ∤ a) the relation is N(c_{mℓ}(a)) = c_m(a)^{1 − σ_ℓ^{−1}}, σ_ℓ the Frobenius of ℓ in Gal(ℚ(μ_m)/ℚ).
sourceIssues.reason: ξ^{−1} − 1 = −ξ^{−1}(ξ − 1), so c_m = −ξ_m^{−1} is a root of unity and z_m = δ(c_m) is torsion; the family is zero after ⊗ ℚ_p and carries no arithmetic. Example 10.2 admits a = −1 among 'a prime to p', which is exactly this degenerate choice. The relation '(1 − ℓ^{−1})c_m' is not defined in ℚ(μ_m)^×; the operator meant is 1 − σ_ℓ^{−1}, as in the corestriction relation and Definition 10.16 that follow.
